summary: Uruguay's Tupamaros, an urban guerrilla group of the 1960s and 70s, robbed banks to aid the poor before the military dictatorship crushed them; member José Mujica survived 14 years in prison and was elected president in 2009.

evidence.note: Raúl Sendic introduced as founder; sugar cane workers march leads him to form the group
first action, the gun club burglary, dated to 1963
Mujica's birth in 1935 and poor childhood near Montevideo
segment on Mitrione, a US police adviser tied to the CIA, kidnapped and executed in 1970
US aid and CIA money flow to the Uruguayan security forces after Mitrione's death
Frente Amplio coalition and the 1971 election, with the Tupamaros backing it
prison conditions under the dictatorship: isolation, beatings, starvation
1984 protests end the dictatorship; amnesty frees the prisoners
Mujica elected president in 2009; reforms and the left's critique of his term

notes: Tupamaros and Mujica treated as co-primary: title names the group, descriptions name Mujica. Colonial and Batlle-era history (1516-1950s) is background and left out of covered_span. reaches_present false: the story mostly stops at Mujica's 2010-2015 term, with only brief remarks on the 2020 government. Covered end is 2021 because Mujica was alive at release (died 2025).
